tldr.text: SOXX +2.33%, IGV +1.65%, XLK +1.00%, QQQ +0.42%, SPY +0.39% on Friday May 22, 2026; semis, AI infra, and quantum rallied while NVDA and select megacap platforms lagged on post‑earnings digestion.
NVDA fell 2.27% despite a large fiscal Q1 beat, AI‑driven data‑center strength, a strong Q2 guide, and an $80B buyback plus dividend hike, as investors digested prior gains.
AI infrastructure, server, networking, and power names (DELL, HPE, SMCI, MRVL, ANET, ETN, VRT) outperformed on hyperscaler 2026 AI capex guidance of roughly $602–$690B.
Quantum computing and related fab names ripped higher after the U.S. Commerce Department outlined a $2B CHIPS Act quantum package including major support for IBM and GFS.

bullets.text: NVDA fell 2.27% to $215.23 despite fiscal Q1 revenue of about $81.6B (+~85% YoY vs ~$79B est.), $75.2B in data‑center revenue (~92% of total), EPS of $1.87 vs ~$1.76–1.77, Q2 revenue guidance of $91B, and an $80B buyback plus a quarterly dividend increase from $0.01 to $0.25.

AMD gained 4.98% to $466.49 as commentary highlighted AI‑driven CPU demand, more than $10B of planned AI supply‑chain investment in Taiwan, and the ramp of Venice CPUs on TSMC 2nm, positioning AMD in the $200B CPU market that Nvidia is targeting.

INTC rose 1.26% to $119.57 as a secondary AI play, with Xeon CPUs selling through held‑back supply, shares more than tripling YTD, and reports of talks to acquire or invest in AI startup Tenstorrent at a valuation above $5B, while ETF weights in SOXX, VLUE, and FTXL added mechanical flows.

Semicap and materials names (ASML, LRCX, AMAT, KLAC, ENTG, UCTT, ICHR, ACMR, VECO, ACLS) moved higher alongside SOXX as rising AI R&D and manufacturing spend and the $125M UCLA AI Semiconductor Hub supported demand for AI‑native hardware and advanced packaging.

MU added 0.65% to $758.94 after announcing 1α DRAM production in Manassas, Virginia as part of a >$2B expansion and $200B U.S. investment plan expected to quadruple DDR4 wafer supply by end‑2026, with consensus looking for EPS to jump from $1.91 to $19.11 and revenue from $9.30B to $33.60B YoY at the next update and management signaling a memory shortage beyond 2026.

Across the AI infrastructure stack, NVDA lagged while CPU, networking, server OEM, and power/cooling names (AMD, MRVL, ANET, SMCI, ETN, DELL, HPE, ORCL, META, VRT) rallied on a Benzinga‑tallied 2026 U.S. hyperscaler AI capex range of roughly $602–$690B.
DELL jumped 17.19% to $296.01 as investors leaned into its positioning as a key AI server beneficiary and upcoming earnings catalyst for major indices.
HPE gained 10.98% to $37.44, rerating with the AI server trade alongside DELL on the same AI capex and infrastructure narrative.

ETN and VRT rose 2.43% and 0.33% respectively as datacenter power, substations, and cooling bottlenecks were flagged as critical constraints in an $8T AI capex cycle of which only 12–18% is currently built.

MSFT slipped 0.19% to $418.07 despite AI exposure amid bearish short‑dated call flow, a $250M Activision shareholder settlement, a GitHub cyberattack investigation, and commentary that Microsoft is pursuing an AI orchestration‑layer strategy rather than a standalone model.
ORCL added 1.05% to $191.43, supported by its role in sovereign AI infrastructure and bullish short‑dated call activity.
CRM climbed 2.94% to $180.76 ahead of Wednesday earnings with the street modeling roughly 12% revenue growth to $11B and BofA framing AI as a key risk versus ServiceNow.
NOW rose 2.28% to $101.40 after BofA reinstated it as a top Buy and called AI a growth engine supporting roughly 20% growth.

SNOW gained 4.84% to $171.94 as a highlighted Nasdaq 100 earnings catalyst, while DDOG, MDB, ESTC, PANW, CRWD, ZS, TEAM, ADBE, and INTU all traded higher with the software and cybersecurity bid amid PT hikes and earnings expectations, including a CRWD PT raise to $700 and detailed ZS estimates.

GOOGL fell 1.70% to $382.40 on reports that the European Commission is preparing a high triple‑digit million‑euro Digital Markets Act fine related to search self‑preferencing following a probe that began in March 2025.
AAPL rose 1.15% to $308.76 even as Japan iPhone 17e unit sales in the first 7 weeks were down 9.8% versus the iPhone 16e, with options flow highlighting active call buying at the $300 strike.

META inched up 0.31% to $608.64 as investors digested news of about 8,000 job cuts, raised 2026 capex to $125B–$145B, launch of a Reddit‑like Forum app, and regulatory scrutiny around WhatsApp encryption and Georgia datacenters.
AMZN slipped 0.56% to $266.76 without a clear tape‑verified catalyst beyond references to AWS Trainium and broader media coverage.
NFLX declined 1.39% to $88.45 despite a BofA Buy rating and $125 PT, while options flow suggested put‑writing via a bullish Sept 2026 $80 put sweep.

UBER dropped 2.54% to $71.95 after reports that its AI budget was effectively exhausted by April due to heavy internal use of Anthropic’s Claude Code and political commentary warning that driverless vehicles could threaten driver jobs.
SPOT rallied 5.49% to $516.23 on multiple PT hikes (including to $650 and $600) and the launch of its “Reserved by Spotify” ticket‑access program with Live Nation.

RBLX gained 2.65% to $47.76 after DA Davidson maintained Neutral but cut its PT to $45, while ad‑ and social‑focused names TTD, PINS, and SNAP traded with the broader tape without specific catalysts in this packet.

NOK jumped 9.27% to $15.44, extending gains as its AI Networking Innovation Lab and FCC approval for in‑home broadband devices were highlighted alongside improving Q2 EPS and revenue expectations and recent analyst upgrades.

MRVL gained 2.71% to $195.01, making a new 52‑week high amid multiple PT hikes tied to AI optical networking and custom ASICs for AWS Trainium and MSFT Maia, though elevated valuation metrics, technical overbought signals, and a large NVDA investment were flagged ahead of its May 27 earnings.
CSCO rose 1.84% to $120.30 despite bearish short‑dated call flow as it was cited as a key supplier in sovereign AI infrastructure alongside major compute and cloud vendors.
ERIC increased 1.81% to $13.48 with sector strength, while a later note referenced plans to relocate its Stockholm HQ to Hagastaden beginning in 2028, described as a long‑term footprint move.
Optical and routing laggards CIEN, LITE, COHR, and AVGO underperformed even as CIEN announced a 400G BNCS‑1 subsea upgrade win and AVGO participated in the UCLA AI Semiconductor Hub.

AMBQ rose 4.99% to $81.00, extending a +117.9% May‑to‑date run after strong Q1 net sales growth and raised Q2 guidance, with over 80% of shipped units running AI algorithms on‑device, underscoring its positioning as an edge‑AI chip name.
NET gained 1.65% to $214.70 with the broader software and AI bid and without a specific company catalyst cited in this packet.
AKAM added 0.90% to $147.13 in line with XLK and IGV moves, also without a distinct single‑name event in the provided materials.

Capital rotated within AI compute as NVDA consolidated post‑earnings while AMD, INTC, ARM, ALAB, CEVA, AMBA, SIMO, and AIP attracted incremental flows, with ARM’s sharp 1‑year and YTD gains, insider sales, and an FTC licensing probe cited as key watchpoints and ALAB’s strong weekly performance alongside insider Form 144 plans highlighted.
AXTI outperformed with a 12.28% gain to $135.79, with the packet flagging only the verified tape move given conflicting narrative references elsewhere.
LASR advanced 3.12% to $78.10 after Stifel maintained a Buy rating and raised its PT from $75 to $85 following better‑than‑expected Q1 results and above‑consensus Q2 guidance.
AMBQ’s move was also framed within the optical and photonics complex as one of the strongest Russell 2000 performers in May, more than doubling MU’s May return.

AAOI increased 1.97% to $179.05 on AI optical transceiver demand, while LITE, LWLG, IPGP, and POET underperformed despite AI capex tailwinds and without ticker‑specific catalysts beyond broad AI infrastructure commentary.

Equipment and materials names ASML, LRCX, AMAT, KLAC, ENTG, UCTT, ICHR, ACMR, VECO, and ACLS each posted gains in the roughly 0.9–4.7% range as investors linked them to AI‑native chip R&D, the UCLA AI Semiconductor Hub, and the broader AI capex ramp.

MU, RMBS, GSIT, MRAM, TSEM, GFS, ASX, AMKR, and UMC mostly traded higher as Benzinga emphasized Micron as a primary AI memory vehicle with sizable ETF weight, heavy upside call activity, and debate over memory‑trade froth even as an $8T AI capex cycle and ongoing HBM shortages were highlighted.
GFS gained 6.28% to $85.67 on a $375M U.S. Commerce CHIPS LOI and ~1% equity stake to scale its Quantum Technology Solutions business plus inclusion in the $2B quantum package and UCLA hub.
ASX climbed 6.62% to $34.81 as a packaging beneficiary of commentary that advanced packaging is a major bottleneck for AI chips and of AMD’s >$10B Taiwan supply‑chain investment plans.
High‑beta memory and IP plays GSIT and MRAM saw speculative demand, with GSIT up 3.39% (intraday +11.7%) and MRAM up 9.14% amid interest in AI memory exposure.

QCOM surged 12.48% to $236.80 on an expanded multi‑year Snapdragon Digital Chassis deal with Stellantis covering cockpit, connectivity, and ADAS chips, building on a prior Q2 beat, dividend hike, and buyback expansion, with options flow showing both bullish June $250 calls and earlier bearish May $250 calls.
MRVL’s 2.71% gain also featured in wireless and mobile as it has become a top S&P 500 AI focus name, up 176% from its YTD low with nine consecutive up weeks.
INDI jumped 13.38% to $4.76, peaking 21.53% intraday, and was framed as a speculative auto and IoT connectivity momentum play without a fresh fundamental catalyst.
RF and mixed‑signal names SWKS, QRVO, SYNA, and HIMX rallied with SOXX and QCOM/MRVL strength, while MXL and AVGO lagged despite AVGO’s role in the UCLA AI Semiconductor Hub.
TXN climbed 4.20% to $309.65 after Seaport Global upgraded the stock from Neutral to Buy with a $400 PT.

ADI rose 3.32% to $396.43 after reporting Q2 EPS of $3.09 vs $2.90 est. on revenue of $3.62B (+37.2% YoY) vs $3.51B est., with valuation and leverage metrics compared favorably on debt but less so on ROE and growth, and a Congressional trade report noting a recent ADI sale and TXN purchase by Rep. Thomas Kean.
NXPI advanced 5.08% to $314.41 as a long‑term compounder with a cited 17.4% 15‑year annualized return that has outpaced the market.
ON gained 6.73% to $116.53 with SOXX strength, though peer‑table metrics highlighted a premium valuation relative to growth.
VSH surged 12.97% to $47.38 as one of the strongest analog movers, while MTSI and POWI posted more modest gains on PT hikes and continued demand signals.

NVTS spiked 18.84% to $29.21 after a May 18 settlement with Live Oak Sponsor that clarified SPAC‑era share overhangs by transferring 726,225 Sponsor Earnout Shares, forfeiting 115,775, and granting a general release.
SMTC rose 6.36% to $154.77 alongside bullish June $200 call activity and an Oppenheimer PT hike to $150 with an Outperform rating.
WOLF closed up 0.30% at $69.77, with intraday data showing an 8.7% move to $75.63 that underscored strong SiC demand.
AEHR gained 5.67% to $94.31 within the wide‑bandgap and test cohort without a specific company catalyst in the packet.

Test and packaging names including CAMT, KLIC, LSCC, PLAB, COHU, FORM, SKYT, ONTO, and TER mostly traded higher with SOXX, with LSCC up 3.49% to $142.99 after Deutsche Bank reiterated Buy and raised its PT from $150 to $175, implying notable upside and helping LSCC outperform the sector.

TSM slipped 0.95% to $403.86 despite a Bernstein PT increase to $430 and commentary highlighting mass production of true 2nm, a forecast 28% EPS CAGR over 2.5 years, and strong AI backlog, as investors appeared to rotate Asian AI exposure toward memory, CPUs, robotics, and infrastructure beyond TSM.
GFS extended gains with a 6.28% move to $85.67 on Commerce’s $375M CHIPS LOI and ~1% equity stake for its Quantum Technology Solutions unit plus quantum‑package and UCLA hub participation.
ASX rallied 6.62% to $34.81 as part of the OSAT and packaging complex tied to AMD’s >$10B Taiwan investments and commentary that advanced packaging remains a major AI bottleneck.
Other fab and timing names TSEM, SLAB, SITM, and UMC saw moves driven by sector dynamics, with Micron‑peer data underscoring TSEM’s richer multiples versus MU’s stronger fundamentals.

Specialty materials and IP names ATOM, GSIT, NVMI, RMBS, OLED, AXTI, and ALMU mostly traded higher with tech, with GSIT again highlighted for double‑digit intraday strength and no major fresh fundamental drivers for most beyond prior‑noted AXTI earnings commentary.

Major tech and growth benchmarks advanced Friday with SOXX +2.33% leading semis, IGV +1.65% in software, XLK +1.00% in tech, QQQ +0.42% on Nasdaq strength, and SPY +0.39% into the long weekend, while there were no additional notable index or ETF decliners in the packet.

The quantum complex rallied sharply with RGTI, QBTS, IONQ, QUBT, and ARQQ posting high‑single to >20% gains alongside GFS, IBM, and INTC after U.S. Commerce detailed a $2B CHIPS Act quantum package that includes about $1B for IBM’s Anderon 300‑mm quantum‑wafer foundry plus awards and equity stakes for multiple players.

callouts.summary: Post‑earnings pullback despite a major beat and raise, highlighting digestion of prior gains and rotation toward broader AI infrastructure and secondary compute plays.
Strength in CPUs and AI positioning driven by commentary on Taiwan investments and Venice 2nm ramp as investors look for alternatives to Nvidia in the AI compute stack.
Shares surged on an expanded multi‑year Snapdragon Digital Chassis deal with Stellantis, reinforcing Qualcomm’s auto and connectivity growth narrative.
AI server exposure and role as an upcoming index earnings catalyst fueled outsized gains within the AI infrastructure trade.
Commerce’s CHIPS Act LOI and equity stake plus inclusion in a $2B quantum package and UCLA hub materially bolstered the foundry’s quantum and AI positioning.
Set to receive about $1B from a new $2B U.S. quantum package to build the Anderon 300‑mm quantum‑wafer foundry, elevating its role in quantum hardware.
Despite being labeled the most trustworthy AI compounder and ramping true 2nm, TSMC traded lower as investors rotated Asian AI exposure into other themes.
Stock weakness reflected reports of an impending high triple‑digit million‑euro Digital Markets Act fine from the European Commission over search practices.
Shares spiked after a settlement with its SPAC sponsor clarified earnout share transfers and forfeitures, reducing perceived overhang.

watch_tomorrow.text: Monitor MRVL into its May 27 earnings following a strong run, multiple PT hikes, and elevated expectations for AI optical networking and custom ASIC growth.
Watch DELL and HPE as key AI server barometers and upcoming earnings catalysts for the Nasdaq 100 and S&P 500 within the broader AI infrastructure trade.
Track CRM and SNOW ahead of their earnings as prominent software and AI sentiment drivers for the Nasdaq 100.
Continue to follow quantum and CHIPS‑linked names such as IBM, GFS, and RGTI after the newly outlined $2B U.S. quantum funding package.
